doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Buying his first flute in Chicago
summary: After trying Yusef Lateef's flute in Detroit, he bought a flute from a stranger in Chicago for thirty dollars.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the first horn: clarinet and saxophone beginnings

blocks.x: One of the things I've always admired about you so much is your ability to play well on all the different instruments. And I think there's a wonderful story behind you getting your first flute that I would love for people to know about.

Oh, I was in Chicago and -- well first of all, before I go there, I was in Detroit one time and we were up at this club where they jammed and Brother Yusef (phonetic sp.) was playing. I forget the name of the club now. And so he was playing flute -­
You're talking about Yusef Latiffe (phonetic sp.)?
Yeah, Brother Yusef Latiffe. Yeah. I'm sorry. So, he -- during an intermission he

said, "Try it." And I picked the flute and I didn't like it. Didn't like it. Couldn't use it. So later on, I was in Chicago -- this is a month after -- and I was drinking a little bit and this guy came up and wanted to sell me a flute, you know. So I think I paid something like thirty bucks for this flute. I didn't even have any money with me because I didn't carry it. Hey, Eddie, you got thirty dollars? Yeah. So I took it and I gave him and I bought this flute. Like oh, I don't know, maybe about two or three months later I made flute (indiscernible). [laughs]
And it was a hot flute too, from what I understand, right?
Well, I didn't want to say that.
